nodes.label: BOE Costing Portal
nodes.rationale: Deliberately self-contained: both services, all configuration, the database schema and a sample Bill of Entry live in one folder so nothing outside it is required to run the system.

nodes.label: Two-Service Architecture (Python parser + TypeScript portal)
nodes.rationale: The TypeScript portal cannot read a PDF. A separate Python process exists for exactly one action (PDF upload); rewriting the x-coordinate extractor in TypeScript would mean re-deriving every watermark, OCR and multi-invoice edge case. The two services are coupled by a single config line, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL.

nodes.label: boe_parser.py - ICEGATE PDF to structured data
nodes.rationale: Called 'the crown jewel'; it is the sole reason a Python service exists at all.
nodes.norm_label: boe_parser.py - icegate pdf to structured data

nodes.label: X-Coordinate PDF Extraction with pdfplumber
nodes.rationale: Extracting by x-coordinate rather than by text flow is what makes the parser survive watermark bleed, OCR spelling variants and multi-invoice numbering.

nodes.label: Manual Entry Bypasses the Backend
nodes.rationale: Manual entry writes straight to Supabase because it is the fallback for when parsing fails - it must not depend on the thing that failed.

nodes.label: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
nodes.rationale: The single seam between portal and parser; pointing it at localhost, Cloud Run or another machine requires no code change.

nodes.label: Supabase Persistence and Key Split
nodes.rationale: Backend and frontend point at the same Supabase project but use different keys: the backend prefers service_role (it runs server-side and Storage uploads need it), the frontend must use anon because that key reaches the browser.

nodes.label: costing.ts - the costing engine
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for the maths; pinned down by 35 tests that need no database.

nodes.label: Landed Costing Model
nodes.rationale: Ported from the C-SHEET of the Excel template the team has always costed against, so portal output stays comparable with the historical spreadsheet.

nodes.label: Value-Proportional Expense Pool Apportionment
nodes.rationale: One expense pool split by declared-value share (Fi/sum F), so changing any expense moves every item's slice in proportion and changing an item's price recomputes the shares before the split.

nodes.label: IGST Excluded from Cost
nodes.rationale: IGST is a creditable input tax, so it is cash flow rather than cost; it is still reported separately as part of the cyber receipt.

nodes.label: Expanded Expense Pool (departure from spreadsheet)
nodes.rationale: The template's I9 = I8+I7+I6+I5 silently dropped Supplier Freight, Bank Charges and Own Bank Charges from cost per piece after displaying them in K6:K8. Including them makes portal figures read higher than the old spreadsheet wherever those are non-zero - that difference is the bug being fixed, not a regression.

nodes.label: Fixed vs Floating Duty
nodes.rationale: A BOE records duty amounts, never rates, so effective rates are back-computed from what customs actually charged. Duty is held fixed by default and may float with value; switching mode with nothing else changed must not move any number, and that invariant is a test.

nodes.label: What-If Scenarios
nodes.rationale: Every scenario input is nullable and means 'inherit the actual', so a new scenario reproduces the actual costing exactly until something is deliberately changed.

nodes.label: FOC Items Keep Declared Value in the Apportionment Base
nodes.rationale: Free-of-charge goods still ship and are still assessed, so keeping their declared value in the base stops freight shifting onto the paid items. A second toggle decides whether duty applies.
nodes.norm_label: foc items keep declared value in the apportionment base

nodes.label: Duplicated Scenario Items Derive Duty from Source Rates
nodes.rationale: Duplicates always derive duty from their source's rates even when duty is fixed, because locking a copy to the source's actual amounts would charge the same customs payment twice.
nodes.norm_label: duplicated scenario items derive duty from source rates

nodes.label: freight_mode is a Label Only
nodes.rationale: Freight can be typed as a total or computed as rate x weight / volume / containers; the Air/Sea label changes no number, so it carries no arithmetic meaning.

nodes.label: No Authentication (open RLS policies)
nodes.rationale: RLS is enabled with fully open policies so the portal works today; anyone with the anon key can read and write. IAP or Supabase Auth is required before this leaves the office.

nodes.label: sql/000_base_tables.sql is a Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Those tables were created by hand and their DDL was never checked in; column names were read back from the live database and types inferred from the code - good enough for a fresh environment but unverified for migrations.

nodes.label: parse_scheme_g misreads quantity as BCD foregone
nodes.rationale: The Part III row matches the column shape the function looks for. Harmless when cash BCD is non-zero, but on a licence-paid BOE it would write the wrong BCD.
nodes.norm_label: parse_scheme_g misreads quantity as bcd foregone

nodes.label: ASSESSED COPY Watermark Bleeds into Descriptions
nodes.rationale: The diagonal watermark injects stray letters into item descriptions (example: 'Super Charger 5AE').
nodes.norm_label: assessed copy watermark bleeds into descriptions

nodes.label: Page Footers Appended to Last Description
nodes.rationale: Example artifact: 'Playmate 2 RemoSte Page 2 Of 7'.
nodes.norm_label: page footers appended to last description

nodes.label: Margin Computed but Not Displayed
nodes.rationale: margin_pct drives sellingPerPiece / totalSelling, which nothing currently renders.

nodes.label: No Excel Export
nodes.rationale: The old Python Excel writer was deliberately not carried over so that costing.ts stays the single source of truth for the maths.

nodes.label: Scenarios Do Not Version
nodes.rationale: Editing a scenario overwrites it; no history is kept.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes against model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is regenerated by next dev, so deleting it only re-creates an uncommitted change - committing it with the work keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: node_modules/next/dist/docs Version Guides
nodes.rationale: Resolved from the AGENTS.md directory rather than the repo root, because in monorepos the next package may not be visible from the root.

nodes.label: frontend CLAUDE.md - @AGENTS.md include
nodes.rationale: Delegates entirely to AGENTS.md so the Next.js-generated rules stay the single copy.

nodes.label: Bills of Entry Are Never Committed
nodes.rationale: A Bill of Entry is a commercial record carrying the importer's address, IEC and GSTIN, the supplier, unit prices and duty amounts - those do not belong in a repository, so the folder is gitignored apart from its README.
nodes.norm_label: bills of entry are never committed

nodes.label: Criteria for a Good BOE Test File
nodes.rationale: A useful fixture exercises the awkward parts: more than one invoice so item numbering restarts at 1, at least one licence-cleared item where cash BCD is 0 and the real figure sits in Part IV Section G, and an ASSESSED COPY watermark that bleeds stray letters into descriptions.
nodes.norm_label: criteria for a good boe test file
